item.text: The reference appears to show a straight-tooth gear with a central bore and a shallow hub on one face. I’ll start with an involute profile along the Y axis, then check the tooth count, thickness, and hub proportions in the preview.
AgentCAD is still processing the detailed tooth sketch. Once it finishes, I’ll use the four-view render to check the gear’s outline and orientation.
The first build is taking longer than expected. I’m waiting for AgentCAD’s result so I can inspect the saved geometry before making any adjustments.

item.text: The detailed sketch timed out, and no geometry was saved. I’ll build one tooth and repeat it around a circular core to make the model more manageable.

The preview matches the 16-tooth layout and places the hub on the correct face. The tooth spaces look too deep, so I’ll increase the core radius and smooth the roots to bring the outline closer to the reference.
The revised outline looks much closer to the reference. I’m rounding the tooth roots, then I’ll validate the single solid and export the STEP file.
